📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

That was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a new manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Recent findings suggest that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

In a recent development, the victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

It has been revealed that newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

Industry observers note that so much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil stated: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

“We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

The draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

Industry observers note that the third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” stated Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is key], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a new coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a big game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We said at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

According to recent reports, moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

According to recent reports, newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

It has been revealed that finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

It has been revealed that free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

According to recent reports, what colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It has been revealed that it’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Industry observers note that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

It has been revealed that millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

Industry observers note that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

It has been revealed that gonzález is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

According to recent reports, hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

According to recent reports, I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

According to recent reports, first piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

In a recent development, barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Sources indicate that wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Recent findings suggest that again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

It has been revealed that murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Industry observers note that newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

The teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

Recent findings suggest that alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach states has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

At the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

The Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Recent findings suggest that jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Sources indicate that aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight fresh signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the new season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

Yunus Musah has insisted that AC Milan must believe in the Scudetto, while also assessing his start to the campaign under Ruben Amorim.

Going into the summer, an uncertain fate awaited Musah. Massimiliano Allegri did not see him as a part of the prepares for 2025-26 and so he was loaned to Atalanta, where he had a mixed year and ultimately returned as they did not use their option to buy him.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Many sources presumed that it would be a return in passing and that a newly introduced destination would be found, but Amorim had other intends. The new coach clearly saw something in the USA international, and he has become a regular starter regardless of the system used.

Industry observers note that such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

“A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”.

Sources indicate that “I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”.

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

According to recent reports, “I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”.

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

In a recent development, “I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”.

Sources indicate that do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

Recent findings suggest that “It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”.

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

What do you remember about America?

“Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”.

Industry observers note that “I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”.

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

Recent findings suggest that “Yes, in 2021 I returned to Upcoming York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”.

Is it true you have a cat named Bronx?

“Yes. I left him with the neighbours in Valencia because I couldn’t take him to Milan.”.

Your family moved from America to Italy….

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”.

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

“Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”.

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

“Of course. Obviously, when I grew up, we weren’t rich, we didn’t have much money, but from the time I left home, even when I was little, my parents never let me go without anything. I hope I’m their pride, because they are mine.”.

You have also played for Arsenal and Valencia. What were the transitions like?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

“I was ready to move to the first team when I was 16, and Valencia had a initiative for me. I spent four wonderful years in Spain; it’s a city that will always remain in my heart.”.

What’s the atmosphere like in the dressing room?

“Last year I watched them a lot; they were a very solid team and difficult to beat. Amorim brought a very positive vibe, we understand each other. He understands the player very well and vice versa.

“It helps when he understands what the players need; he’s good at that, and the players in the team are pretty calm.”.

Is he someone who gets angry when necessary?

“Yes. After Ferencvaros he was very angry, like everyone else.”.

What ties do you have to Africa?

Recent findings suggest that “My wife is from Zanzibar, my family is Ghanaian. So it’s nice to travel to our home countries in the summer.”.

Moises Caicedo has revealed he asked to be substituted at half-time playing for Ecuador as Chelsea were handed a scare during the international break.

Ecuador played friendly matches against Costa Rica and Bolivia, picking up 2-0 victories in both games.

Caicedo played 84 minutes in Quito in what was Marcelo Gallardo’s first game in charge on Saturday, named in the starting XI again on Tuesday.

The former Brighton star was replaced halfway through that game, later revealing he was ‘not feeling well’ with Chelsea’s game against Leeds United on Saturday in his thoughts.

‘No, I didn’t feel very well, so I asked to come off instead, because I know I have another commitment with my club.,’ Caicedo told reporters. ‘So, I’ll try to get there as soon as possible and recover.’.

Caicedo missed Chelsea’s opening game of the season against Fulham, suffering a calf injury 14 minutes after coming off the bench in the following game against Brighton.

He was ruled out of the next three games but has started Chelsea’s last five in the Premier League.

He was also a doubt heading into the game against Sunderland before the international break.

During the international break, the 25-year-old opened up on his recent fitness issues.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘[I’m] a little tired, with some minor issues, but I’m here because it’s my national team and what matters most to me is being here; with my people, with my Ecuador,’ he mentioned.

‘I’m making a major effort to be here, and I’m happy about that.’.

Caicedo is not expected to return to Chelsea training until Friday and will likely have just one session to prove his fitness ahead of the visit of Leeds on Saturday afternoon.

Chelsea return to action sat in fifth place in the English top flight.

A snap 24-hour Tube strike that has shut one line and seriously disrupted another is set to affect passengers heading to events in the capital this weekend.

Members of the Transport Salaried Staffs’ Association (TSSA) working on the Piccadilly Line walked out at noon on Friday in a dispute over the dismissal of a colleague.

As a result the Piccadilly Line was closed and on Friday afternoon there was a part closure and severe delays on the District line.

TfL noted previously due to the shared infrastructure around the Ealing Common District line depot, there will be no service between Earl’s Court and either Richmond or Ealing Broadway from midday on Friday until Saturday evening, with a reduced service on the rest of the line.

TfL says services began to reduce after 10:30 on Friday and will not return to normal on the Piccadilly line until Saturday evening.

The Night Tube will not operate on the Piccadilly line through Friday night. The Night Tube service is expected to operate on Saturday night.

The Elizabeth line, DLR, London Overground, buses and trams are expected to operate as normal during the strike action.

However, these services are likely to be busier than usual as customers seek alternative routes, claims TfL.

Customers travelling to and from Heathrow Airport, as well as those making journeys across central, west and north London, are advised to plan ahead and allow extra time for their journeys.

There are also a number of other planned closures on the Tube and Overground that will cause disruption.

There is a busy day of sport in the capital and disruption on public transport will affect the plans of fans heading to the games.

Lulu was at ex-husband John Frieda’s bedside when he died – on her birthday.

Idina Menzel turns heads in extravagant cape ahead of Royal Variety show.

Londoner charged after ‘knives and other weapons’ seized at busy station.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

Chelsea’s home game against Leeds kicks off at 3pm, with the District line, a popular way of arriving at Stamford Bridge, still expected to be facing severe delays before and after the game.

While fans hoping to use the Piccadilly line as part of their journey to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to watch the 3pm game between Spurs and against Ipswich Town at the will have to find alternatives, which is likely to make other forms of transport very busy.

District line delays could also hinder rugby fans wanting to use it as part of the journey to Twickenham to watch England vs the All Blacks at the Allianz Stadium.

Visitors to do any venues or destinations along the Piccadilly line may have to rethink how they are going to get to and from their destination.

The walkout will have affected anyone wanting to use the line to reach South Kensington to visit the Royal Albert Hall for the Royal Variety performance on Friday night.

Drake Millington plays the Eventim Apollo in Hammersmith on Friday night, normally easy to reach by Piccadilly or District line.

While others hoping to use the line for a night out in the West End, or visit for Christmas shopping or to see the Christmas lights on Saturday will have to rethink their journeys.

Visitors to Winter Wonderland in Hyde Park may also have to rethink their journeys.

On Saturday and Sunday there will be no service between Queen's Park and Harrow & Wealdstone on the Bakerloo line due to track work.

There will be no service between Euston and Watford Junction on the Lioness line on Saturday or Sunday.

No service between Euston and Watford Junction on the Mildmay line on Sunday, with also no service between Camden Road and Stratford after 10.15pm.

On the Weaver line on Sunday there will be no service oin the entire line until 10.15am.

There will be no service between Stratford International and Canning Town on the DLR on Saturday and Sunday.

In a recent development, on Sunday, there will be no service on the Elizabeth line between Paddington and Ealing Broadway until 07:45am due to Network Rail maintenance work. There will also be a reduced service between Paddington and Heathrow/Maidenhead.

Lee Stewart, Transport for London’s head of London Underground service control, said: “We are extremely disappointed that TSSA is proceeding with unjustified strike action in response to the dismissal of an employee working a second job while receiving full sick pay.

“We will do all we can to minimise disruption for our customers.

“I would encourage Piccadilly Line customers travelling on Friday and Saturday to check before they travel and consider alternative routes where possible.

“Our teams will be working hard to keep London moving and provide customers with the information they need to plan their journeys.”.

TSSA general secretary Maryam Eslamdoust visited picket lines on Friday, and noted: “Our members working in service control on the Piccadilly Line are determined to take industrial action in support of their colleague who has been unfairly treated by London Underground.

“We don’t take strike action lightly. Everyone here knows what it costs to lose a day’s pay.

“You’ve come out because you know that every London Underground worker deserves a fair hearing when a staffing matter arises.”.

The walkout is not related to plans for a series of strikes by Tube driver members of the Rail, Maritime and Transport union in a separate dispute over shift patterns.

Their first strike will affect the whole network on November 26 and 27.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:50.

ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.

Their 15-year wait for victory in this fixture further underlines the magnitude of the task facing Maurice Steijn's side.

Ajax entered the recent international break wondering what might have been after surrendering a two-goal advantage at FC Twente.

Goals from Tolu Arokodare and substitute Rayane Bounida seemingly put Michel's men home and hosed heading into the final half-hour, only for Dies Janse to score an own goal and Wout Weghorst to punish his former side with a penalty in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

That equaliser denied De Joden the opportunity to finish gameweek 12 atop the Eredivisie table, leaving them level on 25 points with Feyenoord and one behind leaders PSV Eindhoven, who are chasing a fourth consecutive title.

Looking to move on from that setback, the Amsterdam giants welcome ADO to the capital aiming to secure a seventh consecutive victory over the promoted side.

Further encouraging the hosts is their longstanding unbeaten record in this fixture, with a 3-2 defeat in March 2011 marking Ajax's last loss to this weekend's visitors.

ADO have since gone 20 competitive meetings without a victory in this fixture, losing 15 times to underline their historical inferiority.

As such, it will be intriguing to see how new boss Steijn approaches his first match in charge of the promoted side, who dismissed Robin Peter before the international break following a run of one victory in 11 Eredivisie matches.

There was an immediate lift under Levi Schwiebbe as the second-bottom outfit defeated Sparta Rotterdam 3-1 to move within one point of 16th-placed Telstar in the relegation playoff spot and two of SBV Excelsior.

Back-to-back top-flight victories could therefore lift Den Haag out of the relegation positions, although results elsewhere must also go their way.

Despite the managerial change, ADO's away record offers little encouragement, with the visitors collecting just two points from an available 18 on their travels and failing to score in three of those six matches.

Those figures, coupled with their historical struggles against Ajax, underline the challenge facing Steijn, who is winless in 15 previous encounters with the capital club, losing 11.

ADO Den Haag form (all competitions):.

Ajax could again be without Julian Brandt this weekend, with the attacking midfielder having not played since going off injured in late October's 1-0 victory over AZ Alkmaar.

If the six-goal Germany international remains sidelined, Arokodare, who has seven goals and one assist, will shoulder much of the attacking responsibility, while Oscar Gloukh offers a creative threat with six assists, including setting up both goals in the 2-2 draw at Twente a fortnight ago.

While Anton Gaaei, like Brandt, will be assessed before Sunday, Michel must manage without Simon Adingra, long-term absentee Kasper Dolberg (knee) and Viktor Tsygankov.

Steijn has fewer injury concerns, although the ADO boss must make do without Alex Pozo and Luka Reischl (groin) this weekend.

Juho Kilo may not score regularly, but the midfielder's passing and creativity make him a standout presence for the visitors.

Nonetheless, the goalscoring burden falls on Nigel Thomas, Yannick Eduardo and Evan Rottier, who have netted four, three and two league goals respectively.

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Janse, Wijndal; Amrabat, Baas; Klaassen, Mokio, Gloukh; Arokodare.

ADO Den Haag possible starting lineup:.

Nikiema; De Ruijter, Mulder, Waem, Hokke; Kilo, Jimenez; Van Mieghem, Rottier, Hawkins; Thomas.

Ajax's late collapse at Twente demonstrated that their defensive concentration remains fallible, offering some hope to an ADO side fresh from scoring three against Sparta.

Nevertheless, Gloukh's creativity and Arokodare's finishing should give Michel's men enough attacking quality to overcome Brandt's potential absence and prolong the visitors' miserable record in this fixture.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Santos completed a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer, arriving alongside Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba as the Red Devils sought to bolster their depth in central midfield.
  • Santos enjoyed an encouraging pre-season, but started only four of United’s first ten Premier League matches under Michael Carrick before his sacking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paul Ince still cannot wrap his head around Manchester United’s decision to spend £50million on Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window.

Santos completed a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer, arriving alongside Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba as the Red Devils sought to bolster their depth in central midfield.

Santos enjoyed an encouraging pre-season, but started only four of United’s first ten Premier League matches under Michael Carrick before his sacking.

Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival may represent a fresh start for the £50m midfielder, but Ince believes United would have been better served spending that money elsewhere over the summer.

‘Why did they spend £50m on Santos?’ Ince told The Sun. ‘That’s £50m wasted. They could have put that into the defence or bought a striker.

‘They have [Kobbie] Mainoo, who needs to develop. He needs to be playing, not Santos.

‘Tielemans, again, fantastic at Villa but it’s a different conversation when you come to United.

‘Baleba didn’t play a lot last year. He comes in for £70m, plays a couple of games and he’s injured again.

‘The game’s changing. It’s not all pass, pass, pass now. You’ve got to win your duels. You used to hear Pep Guardiola say every time, “We didn’t win our duels, we didn’t win our tackles”.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game’s more physical, more powerful.’.

United are expected to provide Pochettino with backing to strengthen his squad in the January transfer window.

But Ince fears that his former club will struggle to attract the world’s best talents given their current predicament.

‘What you’ve got is players playing for Manchester United, not Manchester United players,’ he added. ‘That’s a massive difference.

Industry observers note that ‘Who’s a Manchester United player out there? [Declan] Rice, Jude Bellingham. They are who you should be going for.

‘Since Sir Alex Ferguson left it’s been a complete disaster. Would every player in the world want to come to United? They don’t, because it’s a basket case there, a shambles.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi is targeting a move outside of the Premier League despite interest from Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham, according to reports.

Kroupi joined Bournemouth in a £12 million deal from French side Lorient last year and scored 13 goals in his first season in the Premier League.

The 20-year-old has suffered a disrupted start to the new campaign as he required surgery on a foot injury sustained during a pre-season training session in Austria in July.

Kroupi returned in Bournemouth’s 3-0 win away to Manchester United on October 25 and has made three more appearances as a substitute for Marco Rose’s side.

During the international break, Kroupi was handed his senior debut for France as he featured in the 3-1 defeat to Italy, as well as in the 2-1 win over Turkey.

The French striker has attracted interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham, while Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Barcelona have also been monitoring his progress in the Premier League.

However, David Ornstein has claimed that Kroupi will look to move overseas when he leaves Bournemouth, although the club are not looking to sell the forward in the January transfer window.

‘There was a major story recently about Alex Scott possibly leaving in the January transfer window, that was conditional on Bournemouth receiving £100 million and being in a really strong position in the Premier League where that becomes a bit of a no-brainer because in six months’ time he’ll have a year to go on his contract and it’s a very different conversation,’ Ornstein said on The Athletic FC’s podcast.

‘Kroupi has got much longer on his contract for a start, so there’s no massive need to sell in a way you would consider selling Scott.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He’s been out injured for longer as well, so I think Bournemouth want to make use of him this season and they don’t think their chances of recouping significant value in the summer will be much worse than in January, probably better actually.

‘My information around Kroupi is he would like to move at some point, outside of England.

‘You’ve seen very heavy reporting around PSG and Barcelona. If he continues to show the level of form that he was displaying prior to his injury, the biggest clubs in world football want him.

‘It’s no surprise he’s high up on Premier League club recruitment lists, but if what I’m hearing to date is anything to go by, those Premier League clubs may be disappointed because he could be travelling back to warmer climes.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.
  • The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:33 EST, 17 November 2026.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

After previously working as a waitress, Collins transitioned into broadcasting four years ago.

Since starting her career in the media, Collins has had the opportunity to interview a number of sports stars including Frank Lampard.

Recent findings suggest that 'If you receive a message from someone claiming to be me... it’s most likely not. If you don’t have my personal number and are unsure, just DM me on Instagram.

'If you receive anything suspicious, please send it to me directly so I can keep a record of it.

'Thank youuu (purple heart emoji, winking emoji),' she signed off.

Collins has worked in the media since joining IMG Media as an assistant five years ago.

Since 2022, the former waitress has served as a presenter for Premier League productions, which has led to opportunities to interview sports stars including Andy Robertson, John Terry, Bruno Fernandes, Conor Gallagher and Cody Gakpo.

Collins has also worked a number of events beyond the domestic league, such as Wimbledon and the 2025 Champions League final.

This year, she also covered the Open for Sky Sports from Royal Birkdale, and racing at York's Ebor Festival with ITV.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Dutchman, 35, has plied his trade at Anfield since 2018 and is now a two-time Premier League champion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Virgil van Dijk is unsure where he will be playing his football next season, with his Liverpool contract due to expire in the summer.

The Dutchman, 35, has plied his trade at Anfield since 2018 and is now a two-time Premier League champion.

He will be out of contract in June, though, and has revealed in a new interview with Sky Sports that it remains unclear whether he will extend his stay. He is, however, clear that he expects to continue his playing career for several more years.

Per reports from BBC Sport, talks regarding a new deal are underway but an agreement is not close, and no resolution is expected before the new year. From January, Van Dijk will be free to sign pre-contract agreements with clubs outside England.

“The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion,” said Van Dijk.

“Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

“At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.”.

He continued, explaining that he will remain fully focused on on-pitch matters as he awaits clarity on his contract situation.

Sources indicate that “But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the newly introduced year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.”.

He added, matter-of-factly: “If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea should drop their interest in Bournemouth star Alex Scott and turn their attention to a more experienced alternative, according to Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink.

The Blues invested heavily in their squad again during the summer transfer window, but remain light in central midfield where they are heavily reliant on Moises Caicedo following the departures of Enzo Fernandez and Andrey Santos.

Romeo Lavia’s return to form and fitness has represented a welcome boost, but Xabi Alonso is keen to reinforce his engine room further come January.

Scott, who Chelsea attempted to sign in the summer, could well be on the move given his delicate contract situation at Bournemouth.

Arsenal and Liverpool have both been linked with the England international and although Hasselbaink is a keen admirer of the 23-year-old, he feels his old club would be better suited by targeting the Gunners’ out of favour Spain international Martin Zubimendi.

The World Cup winner is yet to start a Premier League game this season amid increased competition as a result of Bruno Guimaraes’ arrival from Newcastle.

Atletico Madrid are understood to have registered their interest in the former Real Sociedad star who is determined to stay and fight for his place at Arsenal, but Hasselbaink believes Chelsea should test the waters.

‘Alex Scott is obviously a top player,’ Hasselbaink told Canada Sports Betting.’He is a player that is getting better with every game that he plays, and he fits with the transfer policy and philosophy of Chelsea because he has serious potential to develop into one of the top midfielders in the world.

According to recent reports, ‘I would prefer somebody with a little bit more experience because we have so many young players in the squad. I think what Xabi Alonso needs is somebody with more experience who is also a top international.

#37733. An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion

An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 41 min read (8151 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~41 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2. This is theorized to happen through common envelope evolution (CEE)3, when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag4,5. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, which originates from the CEE of an approximately 7M⊙ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as an approximately 0.7M⊙ companion inspiralling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven-year period of gradual brighteningone of the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. This phase is radiatively efficient, consistent with predictions for convective transport in CEE5,6,7,8. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core powers the ejection of the outermost 10% of the stellar envelope at speeds about 10× the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope4,9,10,11, 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

According to recent reports, all ground-based optical and near-IR photometry and spectra, together with the JWST and SPHEREx SEDs presented in this paper, are available for download from Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22948026). This repository also contains the bolometric parameters inferred from our SED fits. The JWST images are publicly available through the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (https://doi.org/10.17909/07j6-dq13), and the SPHEREx Quick Release 2 (QR2) images are publicly available at IRSA.

The code used for the analysis of spectra and SEDs used in this paper is available on GitHub at https://github.com/virajkaram/at2025abao/. Any additional code or data can be obtained from the corresponding author upon request.

It has been revealed that near-infrared spectra of AT 2025abao, from its precursor phase (red) and the eruption (blue). The spectra during the precursor phase resemble late M-type stars, while those during the eruption highlights a transition to hotter temperatures. Notably, the CO absorption bands are seen in all spectra, indicating that some molecular gas remains intact even after the eruption.

The black shaded region marks the range expected by varying stellar parameters in the analytical model (section ‘Comparisons to theoretical predictions of enhanced mass loss’). The observed dust mass from the archival progenitor SED and the JWST observation is shown in purple, which constrains the system mass ratio to \(q=0.1{0}_{-0.08}^{+0.10}\).

Previously identified sources such as V1309Sco, M31-LRN-2015, AT 2019zhd (circles) exhibit a gradual brightening by several magnitudes prior to its eruption. AT 2025abao (stars) differs from these sources, as it only shows a bumpy  ≈ 1 magnitude brightening before transitioning to its eruption.

LRNe for which progenitor primary stars have been identified are plotted as coloured points, colour-coded by the binding energy of the star. LRNe with no progenitor identifications are plotted as grey points. The eruption of AT 2025abao (star) is remarkably similar to other LRNe, despite having a progenitor with the lowest binding energy ever measured.

Recent findings suggest that a, The quiescent binary system comprising a  ≈ 7 M⊙ AGB and a  ≈ 0.7 M⊙ star, surrounded by an extended dust shell from mass loss from the binary following Roche Lobe overflow of the primary. b, The precursor brightening phase that began in 2018, marking the onset of CEE, powered by frictional drag on the inspiraling companion lasting for  ≈ 7 years. The mass outflow rate during this phase is  ~10−2 M⊙ yr−1, producing  ~0.1 M⊙ of CBM in an equatorial disk around the binary (dark brown). c, The ballistic eruption in late 2025 from the merger of the inspiraling companion with the primary core, resulting in the ejection of  ≈ 0.1 − 0.2 M⊙ of the primary envelope, and sublimation of a large fraction of dust around the binary. d, The eventual lightcurve powered by shock-interactions between freely expanding merger ejecta (indicated by yellow arrows) and equatorially focused CBM. The surviving pre-existing dust is traced by our JWST observations. The black arrows between the panels indicate the progression of time.

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that James Maddison is still suffering from the same hip issue he sustained during pre-season.

The Tottenham midfielder has started just two games in all competitions this season and has not featured since coming off injured midway through Spurs’ 2-0 victory over Chelsea last month.

Maddison is available for selection against Ipswich this weekend and was also named in the matchday squad in each of Spurs’ last two league games against Crystal Palace and Leeds.

However, De Zerbi’s decision not to bring him off the bench against Palace or Leeds has raised concerns that Maddison is still not fully fit.

The 29-year-old returned from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury at the end of last season, and he had hoped to use pre-season to build his way back to full fitness and force his way into De Zerbi’s starting lineup.

Maddison’s summer was, however, disrupted by setbacks, with a hip matter restricting his ability to train or play with the rest of the squad, and De Zerbi has now revealed that, four months into the season, the same problem is continuing to hamper the England playmaker.

“After Chelsea he had the same injury he felt in the Chelsea game and not a big injury but he was not able to work. He had a problem with his hip,” De Zerbi said in his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

“It’s not a significant problem, but if you don’t work consistently, you lose the physical condition, and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.

“He is still young, 29 years is not old, and he has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.”.

Maddison, who has been unable to train consistently this season, saw his professionalism called into question after Spurs’ defeat to Leeds earlier this month when pictures surfaced of him drinking with friends.

The incident in question occurred on the first of three days off for Spurs’ first-team squad, and De Zerbi says he has no challenges with Maddison’s conduct, instead joking that he was “very angry” that he was not invited.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona have confirmed they have no plans to sell Alejandro Balde and insist the Manchester United-linked left-back remains an ‘notable player’ for the club going forward.

Balde has been with Barca since the age of just eight, making a total of 173 appearances in all competitions since breaking into the first-team squad back in 2021.

In that time, the 23-year-old has helped the Catalan giants win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles – the most recent coming under Hansi Flick last season.

However, Balde has become an increasingly peripheral figure at the Camp Nou in recent months, with all five of his appearances this term coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at Barca and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, this has forced Balde to consider his options and the full-back is understood to be keen on joining Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United in January.

Other reports suggest that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender views the Premier League as a possible escape route.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Obviously, he’s in an uncomfortable situation. The player wants to play.

Sources indicate that ‘He’s one of our own and he’s still an important player. It’s true that he’s not playing right now, although he’s ready if the manager needs him.’.

Deco, Barca’s sporting director, was similarly unequivocal when asked if a transfer deal could be on the cards for Balde.

‘No,’ the ex-Barca, Chelsea and Portugal responded.

‘There is also the player’s side, but he hasn’t told us anything about being unhappy, that’s not the case.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Manchester United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer in order to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, the club’s only specialist in the position other than academy product Harry Amass.

The Red Devils ultimately failed to bolster their full-back options, though, which has come back to bite them already this season, with Shaw sidelined for the last month through injury.

Diogo Dalot was therefore forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back in the bleak final weeks of Michael Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s understood Lewis Hall had been identified as United’s number one left-back target ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, but Newcastle made it clear the England international would not be sold for anything other than an astronomical price.

Hall would go on to put pen to paper on a new long-term deal at St James’ Park, tying him to the Magpies until 2031.

Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell have also been linked in recent months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Barcelona have Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez on their transfer shortlist ahead of the January window, according to reports.

Martinez is into his fifth season at United after signing from Ajax for £57million in 2022.

The Argentine has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the Red Devils, but is out of contract at the end of the season.

United do have the option to trigger a 12-month extension to Martinez’s contract, but they may have reservations after he introduced a scathing public critique of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

And now, Mundo Deportivo reports that Barcelona could be waiting in the wings to pounce as they seek to add a centre-back in the January window.

Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni and Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck are also being considered by the Catalalan giants as options to strengthen Hansi Flick’s side.

But Martinez is viewed as the ‘most economical’ alternative, with the Barca keen on his experience and capability to operate on the left side of defence.

The report adds that Martinez would be willing to listen to an offer, although the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as United’s fresh manager could complicate Barcelona’s pursuit.

Pochettino will take charge of his first match against Liverpool on Sunday, but former Red Devils defender Gary Neville expects Martinez will be one of several defenders to make way in the coming transfer windows.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.

Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but says he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.

The scrutiny cast upon him by the watching world led to Rooney hitting 'rock bottom' in his mid-twenties, whereby he recalls locking himself away in his house for two days to 'just drink'.

According to recent reports, 'This was at the best part of my career playing wise, I'd go home and sit in my games room and drink for two days,' he noted on Life At The Midpoint podcast. 'I'd get up for training, put some eyedrops in and chewing gum, and go to training.

Recent findings suggest that 'I couldn't deal with the pressures of everything and I made stupid choices when I was younger, off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all to be honest. It was only when I spoke to Coleen and I spoke to my mum, and I opened up, it was only really when I vocally opened up that I needed help to get through it.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how he contemplated suicide during his 'lowest' moment.

He said without the support of wife Coleen, he may not have 'survived' as he discussed how his life turned upside down after breaking through as a 16-year-old.

The Man United legend noted he was binge-drinking for two days at the height of his career.

'When I look back now, you look back with regret because it's time lost. Kai was a baby at the time. I can look back and say I was selfish but I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

Industry observers note that 'I got to a place where I was contemplating suicide. I didn't want to be around anyone, I didn't want to see anybody in the street, in the shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else I struggled with.'.

Rooney added that his drinking problem caused strain on his marriage to childhood sweetheart Coleen, but he couldn't have survived without her help.

'Coleen helped me massively,' Rooney said. 'I was speaking to a therapist to figure out what was up with me. Looking back, I was at the height of my career, just had a young son, just married, it should have been the happiest moment of my life but it was the lowest, because of the selfish acts I was taking.

According to recent reports, 'Coleen was massive. She could have walked away, it was that bad. She stuck by me and helped me get through it and obviously we had more kids.'.

Rooney also spoke candidly about his anxieties over his appearance.

The former Man United and England striker has overhauled his lifestyle, slimmed down, fixed his teeth and undergone a nose job, with fans amazed by his progress.

When asked about how he felt about the prospect of being exposed to a huge audience of viewers in the I'm A Celebrity jungle, Rooney admitted it was something he only now feels comfortable with after his glow-up.

'I wouldn't have been able to do it to be honest with you,' he told Gabby Logan on Life at the Midpoint podcast.

According to recent reports, 'They asked me last year to go in. I spoke to AngryGinge who I know and Aitch who I know and they were saying, "come in, imagine the three of us in there". It would have been chaos. I didn't think I'd physically be able to do it.

Wayne Rooney, pictured left on I'm a Celebrity and right in 2024, has admitted he used to feel self-conscious about his looks and weight.

Should footballers receive more support for mental health given pressure they face?

'I've always been self-conscious and always been conscious of my weight. I've always thought about how I look.

'Everything has fallen into place now where I know I feel better and know I look better than what I was. I looked at myself about a year ago and thought I did look probably about 50.

'And I was thinking, "you need to sort yourself out here" and so I was very self-conscious. I have been for my whole career for how I look or my weight, which at times I've struggled with.'.

Rooney had to endure a stomach-churning eating challenge on the launch show on I'm A Celebrity on Monday night, drinking fermented prawns and fish eyes and no doubt there's worse to come.

The slimmed-down Rooney was previously irked that some onlookers thought he had been taking weight loss injections rather than working hard to get in shape.

It has been revealed that he previously explained to the Daily Mail: 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing (weight loss jabs). It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'.

It has been revealed that he added on This Morning: 'I feel great, I haven't drank for a while. I just wanted to feel healthier and be healthier so I've changed my eating habits and training.

Industry observers note that 'Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing. but I'm not, I've been working out to try and look better and be healthier.'.

Rooney has been praised for his physical turnaround and is favourite to win the show.

Rooney, pictured two years ago, cut down his drinking and changed his lifestyle.

He also stated part of the motivation was to feel better for his time with the family. Rooney and his wife, who came second on I'm A Celebrity two years ago, are parents to Kai, 17, Klay, 13, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.

'I've found more balance, it's helped me get back to a much better place. When I stopped playing, I got in a rut, I was drinking too much and not getting into the routine of training and I just thought, "You know what I want to enjoy the time with the kids whilst they're at this age, and with Coleen as well and I actually have been more present, more there for them,' he added.

At times during his playing days, Rooney was far from the model professional and back in 2012 admitted returning to Man United training seven pounds overweight.

In his book, My Decade in the Premier League, Rooney wrote of the summer of 2009: 'Early July: the first day back at pre-season training. I'm like most blokes, I put on a few pounds after a holiday. Even if I don't train for a week, I put on two or three, but when I get back to Carrington for the first day of work, I'm in for a shock. The scales in the club gym tell me I've put on a few more pounds than expected – seven. Seven!

In a recent development, 'Then I remember – I drank a few bevvies while I was away. I'm stocky. I'm not like Ryan Giggs, all bone and lean muscle. But I gain weight quite easily. It's not a problem though.

According to recent reports, 'It's not as if the manager is leaning over my shoulder as the numbers come in, tutting and making jokes about me eating too many chip butties. Besides, I know I can shift it in a week or two. All the players are given loose training programmes to stick to while they're away, but they're optional.

'The club like us not to go overboard on the eating and drinking in the close-season break, so if I go abroad I like to get into the hotel gym three times a week to work on the treadmill and do some weight work.

'Coming back for pre-season after a few bevvies and a few weeks away from a ball is physically tough.'.

Despite Rooney's penchant for letting his hair down in the offseason, he was renowned for his work and commitment on the pitch and has recaptured that battling spirit to shed the weight in retirement.

Rooney, pictured during a match against Portugal at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, was not always fully committed to his diet during his glittering playing career.

The England legend has emerged as the betting favourite to be crowned King of the Jungle and is one of the highest-paid contestants in this year's show.

Bosses have reportedly offered Wayne more than his wife, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint.

Last week, Rooney said: 'This is probably the biggest exposure I've ever had, being on TV every night for three weeks.

'I hope people see I am a genuine person,' adding that he is a 'fun guy' who enjoys 'pranks'.

No doubt his dieting will be beneficial in having to deal with rations of long grain rice and beans in Australia for the duration of the show.

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 20:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:00.

In a recent development, coventry City vs. Crystal Palace is the sort of match that will keep Frank Lampard's men in the Premier League if they can prevail, an ex-Sky Blues striker has told Sports Mole.

Coventry host Crystal Palace in the Eagles' first fixture under new head coach Thomas Frank, who takes over from Pierre Sage with the Eagles languishing at the bottom of the Premier League table.

The hosts, meanwhile, are three places and two points better off in the relative safety of 17th spot, having taken nine points from their opening 10 games of their first top-flight season in 25 years.

Two of Coventry's three league triumphs this season have come at the CBS Arena, both against bottom-half rivals in Newcastle United and Sunderland, although Fulham and Hull City have also got the better of them in front of their own fans.

Former Coventry striker Mark Hateley - who scored 27 goals in a century of appearances for the Sky Blues - is fearing a latest manager bounce for Palace, but warned his old club that this type of match could dictate their survival chances.

Recent findings suggest that “You always get that bounce from a upcoming manager," Hateley noted. "You get it for one, two, three games, and then it starts to wear off. Thomas Frank is a proven tactician who sees things very promptly within a team.

In a recent development, “Palace still have a really decent side with decent players, so I think he'll be in and about it rapidly, and you'll see a style of play that he gets from what he sees in that group of players. Whether it lasts all the way through, I don't know, but I think he'll fix Palace into a side that will be OK.

“Coventry are the other side. They've got to survive this year and build for the next two years: survival, survival, survival. Palace will know how to do it; they've got good enough players. But these are the games Coventry should be looking to win. These are the games that keep you in the league.”.

Saturday's match will mark the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal Palace since the 2011-12 Championship season, when the Sky Blues lost 2-1 away before holding the Eagles to a 1-1 draw at home.

Coventry earned their most recent victory against Crystal Palace shortly beforehand, prevailing 2-1 in February 2011 thanks to goals from Richard Wood and Marlon King.

Taking data across all competitions from Lampard's Coventry tenure so far and Frank's lengthy spell at Brentford from 2018 to 2025, the statistics somewhat favour the Chelsea legend.

Indeed, Lampard boasts more points per game, more goals scored per match and fewer goals conceded per match, while also winning one trophy in the form of the Championship.

However, those numbers must certainly be taken with a pinch of salt given Frank's substantially longer spell at Brentford, and the Dane's four full seasons in the top flight after winning promotion with the Bees.

Industry observers note that lampard's Coventry have nevertheless shown promising signs after he also succeeded in keeping Everton afloat in the top flight, though, so Saturday's edition of Frank vs. Frank is a challenging one to call.

Mark Hateley was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of London.bet.
