Industry observers note that the effect of this strong reconstruction on the band structure involves two ingredients: (1) the PMF and (2) variations of the local work function across the moiré plaquette35. We first calculated the band structure for the reconstructed AB and AA configurations, excluding the variations in work function (Fig. 5g,i). Two features emerge: (1) a substantial bandgap is opened owing to the reconstruction-induced difference between the on-site potential of each carbon sublattice35,36,37; (2) several fourfold spin-valley degenerate flat bands appear within the bandgap (Supplementary Information Sections 29, 31 and 32). Plotting the corresponding real-space wavefunctions (inset colour maps in Fig. 5g,i) reveals their localization at the vertices of the moiré domain AB-2, AA-1 and AA-2, in which strain and the PMF both peak. These flat bands can be interpreted as PLLs arising from the PMF. In reciprocal space, they are manifested as flat bands that host strongly localized electrons25. Equivalently, we can view them as strain-induced quantum dots situated at the moiré-domain vertices. Notably, because the zeroth PLL in graphene sits at the NP and is only half-filled, it cannot change the doping level unless its energy is shifted and hybridizes with either the valence or the conduction dispersive bands.

In a recent development, taking into account the work-function landscape across the moiré plaquette (owing to local strain and van der Waals environment) shifts the flat bands away from the bandgap, hybridizing them with either the valence or the conduction bands and thus resulting in doping of graphene. The curvature at the AB-2 site lowers the hybridization of the pz orbital of carbons (similar to carbon nanotubes38), increases the local work function at AB-2 and consequently shifts its corresponding flat band downward (Fig. 5h). Conversely, the in-plane strain at AA-1 and AA-2 vertices reduces the carbon–carbon distance, resulting in the reduction of the local work function and upward shift of the corresponding flat bands39 (Fig. 5j). Other factors, such as the van der Waals environment, contribute with the same trend35,37 (Supplementary Information Section 27; Supplementary Figs. 43–45).

According to recent reports, the resulting work-function variation lowers the flat bands towards the valence band in the AB configuration and raises them towards the conduction band in AA (Fig. 5h,j). Once the empty/filled flat bands in the AB/AA configuration cross the valence/conduction band, the holes/electrons trapped in the corresponding quantum dots are released into the body of the moiré domain and start to contribute to transport. This shifts the Fermi level away from the neutrality point to the valence/conduction bands and the AB/AA configuration will demonstrate p-doping/n-doping, respectively. In this picture, electrons are redistributed between the conductive moiré domain and the insulating quantum dots at its vertices.

Recent findings suggest that hole-side angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements corroborate this picture. Comparing the mhBN/graphene/hBN heterostructure against a conventional graphene/hBN reference region on the same flake (Fig. 5k,l), a flat band (orange) appears exclusively in the mhBN region and hybridizes with the neighbouring dispersive band (red), consistent with our above picture.

It has been revealed that such a doping mechanism explains the observed integer charging per moiré plaquette. In the simplest picture, each PLL holds g = gsgv = 4 states (spin × valley degeneracy). In the AB configuration (Fig. 5e), this condition is met at only one vertex per plaquette. Because the zero-energy PLL is initially half-filled, each vertex accommodates two more electrons (or holes), giving n/n0 = +2 for the initial p-doped state (blue sweep in Fig. 2d); in the AA configuration, two vertices contribute, giving n/n0 = −4 (red sweep). This accounts for the p-doping before the transition being consistently smaller than the n-doping after it.

Building on the above simplest picture, understanding such integer quantization also requires fundamental energy balance considerations. A well-established physical principle for structural stabilization seen in phenomena ranging from the Peierls transition in one-dimensional crystals to the filled shells of noble gases is as follows: when energy spectra are discrete, configurations with fully occupied and fully empty states separated by a gap become energetically favoured. In our system, the necessary discrete spectrum arises not from atomic orbitals or external magnetic fields but from PLLs generated by the strong periodic strain of the moiré reconstruction. Crucially, this solid-state system has a tunability absent in atomic prototypes: it can tune the electrostatic energy directly by solid gate and self-optimize the energy spectrum to maintain integer fillings. Similar to flux optimization in GaAs quantum rings40, the system can adjust the PMF strength (through strain redistribution) to ensure that the PLL degeneracy exactly matches the electron occupancy. The finite energy gain from fully occupying a Landau level compensates for the extra elastic deformation costs, effectively locking the system into a stable, integer-quantized state. We note that this self-optimization operates at the local scale involving only small strain variations around moiré vertices. This local self-optimization is distinct from the global structural transition itself, which is driven by the competition between van der Waals, elastic and electrostatic energies (Fig. 4).

Further evidence identifying commensurate filling of the discrete PLL spectrum as the origin of the integer doping, and ruling out alternative scenarios (charge trapping, Coulomb blockade of moiré-potential quantum dots, interfacial ferroelectricity and contact electrostatics), is provided in Supplementary Information Section 39.

It has been revealed that we believe that our work opens a upcoming avenue for engineering structural and electronic phase transition in dynamical van der Waals systems through careful balancing of Coulomb, van der Waals and elastic energy contributions. Structures with several aligned interfaces can result in more complex phase transitions and electronic states. We also point out that the periodic arrangement of localized PLLs demonstrated here constitutes a regularly distributed array of quantum dots defined by strain. This connection to quantum dot physics opens avenues for further fundamental and applied investigations. Notably, such integer doping and phase transition occur across a broad range of moiré sizes (from 6 nm to 17.7 nm), eliminating the requirement for precise twist angle control in sample fabrication.

Sources indicate that heterostructures were assembled using the standard dry-transfer technique. Two device architectures were used: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN, in which the mhBN–hBN interface was intentionally misaligned by 15° to ensure superlubricity, and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN. Seven more types of reference device were fabricated by the same process (full list and data in Supplementary Information Section 4). The sample types are categorized by alignment and hBN thickness. The alignment scenarios include double alignment (a), single alignment (b), top and bottom hBN aligned with each other but not with the encapsulated graphene (c), single alignment with unencapsulated graphene (d) and a nonaligned three-layer stack (e). Samples with the same alignment are further subdivided by hBN thickness (bulk, bilayer and monolayer hBN), as illustrated in the schematics in Supplementary Fig. 7, into a1–a4, b1, b2, c1, d1 and e1. The a2 and a4 samples are the devices used in Fig. 2, listed in Supplementary Tables 1 (samples 1–8) and 2 (samples 9–10). Other sample types are for reference with data in Supplementary Information Section 4.

For the non-capped (single-gated) samples, simultaneous alignment of graphene to both hBN crystals was confirmed by AFM and transport measurements: the Fourier transform of the AFM topography (inset of Fig. 2b) indicates two moiré periodicities of 10.8 nm and 12.0 nm (ref. 19), corroborated by the two sets of secondary Dirac points in the transfer curves13,14,15,41 (Fig. 2d). For the dual-gated encapsulated samples, in which the two moiré patterns are practically identical in size and the secondary Dirac points coincide in gate voltage, double alignment was confirmed primarily by Raman spectroscopy combined with optical imaging and AFM (ref. 42). Detailed analysis is given in Supplementary Information Section 2. The thickness of the hBN layers (down to monolayer) was confirmed by Raman and AFM measurements (Supplementary Information Section 2).

Transport measurements were performed in a TeslatronPT cryostat at a base temperature of T = 1.6 K, equipped with a superconducting magnet providing fields up to 14 T. Longitudinal and Hall resistances were measured in a four-terminal configuration using standard low-frequency lock-in SR860 lock-in amplifiers, with an AC excitation current of 5 nA at 37 Hz to avoid sample heating. Gate voltages were applied by a Keithley 2601 source meter. For dual-gated devices, the top-gate and back-gate voltages were swept simultaneously along the D = 0 line30 unless stated otherwise. The critical transition voltage is independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15); control experiments excluding contamination and other artefacts are detailed in Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14.

The stability, work function, electronic structures and charge transfer of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures have been thoroughly studied using DFT calculations. Our calculations are based on the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional as implemented in the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The interaction between the valence electrons and ionic cores is described within the projector augmented-wave approach with a plane-wave energy cut-off of 500 eV. The widely used semi-local approximations for the exchange-correlation energy do not take long-range correlations into account correctly. Thus, they fail to reproduce van der Waals attraction and the prediction of equilibrium geometries of van der Waals bound layered systems. To address the problem, the dispersion correction schemes proposed by Grimme were used to treat the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN layers. The Brillouin zone was sampled with the Monkhorst–Pack grid and the grid sizes depend on the size of the supercells used. The grid was chosen to be as dense as 31 × 31 × 1 for a primitive cell and Γ-point only for a large supercell of near 5 nm. The vacuum space of at least 15 Å was used to avoid interaction between neighbouring layers. In the structural energy minimization, the atomic coordinates are allowed to relax until the forces on all of the atoms are less than 0.01 eV Å−1. The energy tolerance is 10−6 eV.

Because full-scale DFT calculation would be computationally unrealistic for a moiré unit cell consisting of 56 × 56 atoms of graphene monolayer and at least twice the 55 × 55 atoms of two hBN layers, we would investigate the structure using a combination of DFT calculations and empirical potentials MD simulations. For specified stacking of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures, calculations were done using the commensurate structure with the graphene lattice. To understand the adhesion energy and the work function distribution of the moiré structure, we screen the local stacking of the moiré cell of hBN/graphene/hBN using a 21 × 21 grid of sampling points. The structure at each sampling point was obtained by shifting the graphene with respect to the hBN layers on the two sides. To model the gate-induced electron doping in graphene, extra electrons were added to the supercell and a uniform positive charge background was added to compensate and ensure the charge neutrality of the system.

Sources indicate that the structure relaxations were implemented in the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). We used many-body Tersoff potentials to treat the in-plane C–C and B–N interactions. The interlayer van der Waals interaction between the graphene and hBN was described by the registry-dependent Kolmogorov–Crespi potential. To model the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN under gating, we vary the strength of the C–B interaction relative to the C–N interaction using a scaling parameter (s). We found that, for s = 5% and s = 50%, the potential is qualitatively consistent with the DFT interlayer adhesion of the trilayer heterostructure in the absence and presence of doping, respectively. Using the s = 50% scaling of the C–B/C–N interaction, we successfully simulated the structural transition of the heterostructure. To include the substrate effect of bulk hBN and model the interlayer interactions among different boron nitride layers, we proposed a Lennard–Jones 6–12 potential to describe the repulsive and attractive terms, and Coulomb’s law is used for the electrostatic interactions. This yields.

Sources indicate that in which ϵij and σij are the potential parameters to control the strength of the attractive and repulsive interactions, respectively, rij is the interaction distance between atom i and atom j, qi and qj are the atomic partial charge in units of the elementary charge and Kc is the coulombic constant. We set 0.2 and −0.2 for the B and N, respectively after careful evaluation. Because of the smaller van der Waals radius of B (about 1.92 Å) and large interlayer distance of hBN layers (about 3.30 Å), we neglected the short-range B–B interactions in this study. ϵBN and ϵNN were set to 0.3035 and 10.8237 meV, respectively. Also, we used 3.75 and 3.1461 Å for σBN and σNN, respectively. During the simulation, the cut-off distance was set to 8 Å for the attractive and repulsive terms. A long-range solver of the standard coulombic Ewald summations was used to compute long-range coulombic interactions or long-range interactions. The atomic structures were equilibrated using the NVT ensemble (canonical ensemble). A 2.0-ns annealing process from 300 K to 1 K was first carried out and then the other 0.5-ns timescale was implemented to stabilize the structures. A time step of 1.0 fs was used and the relaxation was completed when the forces are less than 10−6 eV Å−1. The unrotated heterostructures were modelled by 56 × 56 unit cells of graphene and 55 × 55 unit cells of hBN, resulting in a 1.8% mismatch in lattice constant. We used four monolayers of hBN to imitate bulk substrate, in which the bottom two layers were fixed and the top two layers allowed relaxation during the MD simulations.

Industry observers note that the lattice structures of graphene and hBN are incommensurate; although both feature a honeycomb lattice (graphene of carbon atoms and hBN of boron and nitrogen atoms), the hBN lattice period is δ ≈ 1.8%, longer than that of graphene, a = 0.246 nm. Including an anticlockwise twist of the hBN layer, θ, the interference of the two lattice potentials at the interface gives a moiré superlattice, magnified from the graphene lattice, with moiré superlattice period \(\lambda \approx a/\sqrt{{\delta }^{2}+{\theta }^{2}}\), and rotated by φ ≈ −arctan(θ/δ). The moiré superlattice Bragg vectors are constructed as linear combinations of the ‘first star’ of non-zero vectors, Gm ≈ δ · gm − θ(ez × gm) m = (0, 1,…, 5), expressed in terms of the first star of graphene vectors, \({{\bf{g}}}_{{\rm{m}}}=\frac{4\pi }{\sqrt{3}a}\left(-\sin \frac{m2\pi }{3},\cos \frac{m2\pi }{3}\right)\), and depicted alongside the moiré Brillouin zone.

Aston Villa took a "big step forward" in their 0-0 draw with Sunderland, so claims Unai Emery.

Villa drew a third straight Premier League match as they were frustrated by the Black Cats at Villa Park.

It is the first time Villa have drawn three straight Premier League games since 2014.

Villa attempted 700 passes in this match – their most on record (from 2003-04) in a single Premier League game, completing 624, their joint-most on record (also v Hull City in September this season).

Sources indicate that they had 19 shots, but those chances were worth only 0.98 expected goals (xG) combined. Emery, though, was pleased with the levels demonstrated by his team on the occasion of his 150th Premier League game in charge of Villa.

Emery told Sky Sports: "A little bit frustrated, but how we are building our team and recovering our confidence in our style of playing, [this game] was a step forward.

"We were dominating, we were progressing with passes, and we were in a good position to control the game, but we didn't create many clear chances.

Industry observers note that "But this is the way and the idea we have to try and implement. We avoided the moment of them dominating us and avoided giving up chances to the opponent. We did a lot of good things.

In a recent development, "It is not enough, but we know how we have to try and build the team and how we can feel better. One step forward, clear in the style. Keep going forward.".

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.

Sources indicate that daniel Farke’s team conceded six here earlier this season. That wild defeat in the Carabao Cup in September came at a time when Chelsea were playing cavalier football that made a 6-3 scoreline seem normal, but they stand now on the brink watching their season fall apart.

This was not what their supporters were sold when Xabi Alonso was appointed amidst broad smiles six months ago.

The leadership spoke then of lessons having been learned and of a corner turned. What must co-owner Behdad Eghbali and his four-strong team of sporting directors have made of Leeds running rings around their team on their own pitch, cantering to an easy victory with minimal resistance?

They began well here, 23-year-old striker Emmanuel Emegha firing them ahead early on his full debut, but within minutes they had gifted Okafor an equaliser, a lovely finish into the corner facilitated by static Chelsea defending.

Morgan Rogers might have been unfortunate to concede the penalty at the start of the second half, which was converted by the excellent Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but that decision was not the reason Chelsea were beaten so soundly.

Chelsea player ratings vs Leeds: Palmer anonymous as Blues humiliated.

Chelsea handed fresh injury blow as Caicedo forced off against Leeds.

Industry observers note that who is Olutayo Subuloye? Chelsea youngster on bench for Leeds clash.

Make 2026 the year of working smarter.

Okafor rapidly made it three for Leeds, Branden Aronson got a fourth in stoppage time, as Chelsea slumped into mid-table.

Recent findings suggest that leeds were quickly on the front foot and might have lead early. A wonderful cross from James Justin was met by Calvert-Lewin, ghosting between two defenders to head against the crossbar.

Moises Caicedo was forced off after 20 minutes after a landing awkwardly, arguably the point at which the hosts began to lose their way. Calvert-Lewin soon found room again amongst Chelsea’s defence for a header that was this time straight at Emiliano Martinez.

Industry observers note that emegha’s goal was Chelsea’s only bright spot. Justin made a mess of a clearing header and gave it to Rogers, who nipped past Nico Elvedi and slipped it left for Emegha to take a touch and finish like a striker that had been crashing them in at the Shed End for years.

The manner in which Chelsea let Leeds back level two minutes later will have infuriated Alonso. Josh Acheampong misjudged the bounce of the ball in midfield and Calvert-Lewin stole in and fed Okafor.

There were then three defenders in blue standing motionless around Okafor inside the box as he took aim and rolled the ball into the corner of Martinez’s goal.

A wonderful Calvert-Lewin back-flick was inches from putting Leeds ahead. A goal then would have not unfairly reflected the balance of the first half. Chelsea were a mess and were booed off at the break.

According to recent reports, it took an age for VAR to determine that Michael Oliver had been correct to call handball against Rogers from Jayden Bogle’s driven effort in the 48th minute. Rogers had motioned towards the ball which cannoned away of a combination of upper arm and shoulder, but Chelsea felt aggrieved. From the spot, Calvert-Lewin sent Martinez the wrong way.

Okafor whacked in his second and Leeds’ third just before the half-hour, a deflected cross sitting up for a lovely half-volley into the top corner.

Now was the time for another two-goal Chelsea fightback as on that bizarre night in September. Predictably, it never materialised, only another goal from Aronson and more boos for Alonso’s players at the end.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • According to recent reports, but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

According to recent reports, but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

According to recent reports, united were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Recent findings suggest that afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical strategy to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s latest head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their newly introduced head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

According to recent reports, was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

Sources indicate that there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

It has been revealed that even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

Thomas Frank suffered defeat in his first game as Crystal Palace boss as Dwight McNeil’s late own goal condemned them to a 3-2 loss at Coventry.

Frank, who was sacked by Tottenham in February, oversaw his first game for a third London club but was unable to stop them from losing for a fifth successive match in the Premier League.

Frank’s tenure got off to the worst start possible when Taiwo Awoniyi put the hosts in front with his second goal of the campaign, but Palace instantly responded through Yeremy Pino.

An all-action first half continued as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s sublime strike put Coventry back in front before Jorgen Strand Larsen’s first goal since September pulled Palace level again.

It looked like Palace would come away with a point until McNeil inadvertently bundled the ball into his own net to secure Coventry back-to-back home wins.

Frank Lampard’s side are growing in confidence in front of their own supporters and picked up a third win at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

Frank calls Arsenal cup gaffe while at Tottenham a ‘fantastic story’.

Lampard was wary of the visitors starting strongly with a newly introduced boss, but it was his side who drew first blood when Jack Rudoni played the ball across for Awoniyi to stab a first-time effort into the far corner.

The hosts were left wondering how they were not two to the good when, seconds after Carl Rushworth’s save down one end, the Sky Blues broke through Awoniyi and he rounded Dean Henderson but saw his effort blocked heroically by Axel Disasi on the goal-line.

They were made to pay shortly afterwards as Palace levelled.

Daichi Kamada sent a cross in towards Strand Larsen who saw his failed scorpion attempt bounce kindly for Pino and he lashed home from close range.

Coventry regained their advantage on the half-hour mark courtesy of a sublime hit by Sakamoto.

Rudoni had assisted the first and was the creator again as he whipped a cross to Sakamoto who took a lovely touch with his chest before lashing a shot past Henderson from outside the box.

It has been revealed that palace came from behind for a second time on the stroke of half-time. Pino turned creator with a cross onto the head of Strand Larsen, who had sprung the offside the trap and nodded the ball beyond Rushworth.

Henderson was called into action to stop Coventry from going ahead for a third time as he dived to his right to palm Rudoni’s effort behind.

Palace were in the ascendancy and looking most likely to get their noses in front.

Strand Larsen was first onto a low cross by Pino but he was stopped by Rushworth and Bobby Thomas made a crucial block to stop substitute Evann Guessand from sweeping the ball home.

It proved vital as Coventry snatched a winner. Brandon Thomas-Asante’s initial header was saved by Henderson but the ball bounced off McNeil and rolled over the line.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti will take charge of his 600th Serie A match as a manager against Venezia, and he is approaching it the same way he did his first.

Spalletti will become the sixth manager to reach this milestone in the competition's history, after Carlo Mazzone (792), Nereo Rocco (747), Giovanni Trapattoni (689), Gian Piero Gasperini (648) and Nils Liedholm (635).

Juventus have had a topsy-turvy season so far, but are unbeaten in their last two league matches, twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 with Fiorentina following a 2-0 win over Napoli.

And Spalletti will be keen to mark his landmark match with a victory.

"I am preparing with the same emotion as I did for my first in Serie A," he noted about his landmark match.

"There were moments during this journey that marked my career as a coach. I'm very happy to have had this tour in football, because it was my life and what I always wished for.

"I learned to be happy even when things are not going in my favour, and I hope to keep going for as long as possible.".

Juventus sit seventh in the league with just 18 points after 11 games, with suggestions they could miss out on Champions League qualification for the second season running, but Spalletti is not yet worried.

"I do think we have that possibility, but our objective is to become something," Spalletti said when asked about their start to the season.

Sources indicate that "If we do that, then we can get good results and a strong position in the table. We have to rely on our work; we want to create habits for constant improvement.".

It is fitting that Spalletti's landmark match is against Venezia, whom he coached at the start of his career, though he was sacked twice in the space of one season in 1999.

Sunday's visitors to the Allianz Stadium sit 19th, with only six points so far, and they have lost each of their last six Serie A away games, but Spalletti had high praise for the team.

"I have fond memories of a melancholic but splendid city," Spalletti added of his time at Venezia. "Those were my first seasons. I had strong Presidential and directorial figures; the team was struggling, so I was fired and brought back.

Industry observers note that "I want to congratulate Davide Nicola, as wherever he goes in his career, he brings a solution to problems and fuels enthusiasm. They'll try to strangle us and then send strong strikers on the attack like Akor Adams, so balance is essential.".

After an assist against Fiorentina and a goal and an assist against AZ, Randal Kolo Muani could be involved in a goal in three consecutive club appearances in all competitions for the first time since between May and June 2025.

That was also for Juventus when he got a goal against Venezia in Serie A, a brace against Al Ain and an assist against Wydad Casablanca in the Club World Cup.

Since Serie A returned to a 20-team format in 2004-05, Antoine Hainaut (four – two goals, two assists) is the first Venezia defender to have a goal involvement in more than three goals in a single top-flight season.

He set up Toma Basic's opener against Udinese before the international break, but also led that game in shots (four) and touches in the opposition box (six), alongside his two chances created.

Juventus are unbeaten in their last 14 Serie A matches against Venezia (W11 D3), with the Winged Lions' last victory against the Bianconeri dating back to April 1962 (3-0 at the Penzo).

In fact, Juventus have never lost in 14 home Serie A games against Venezia (W11 D3).

Among the teams currently in the top-flight, Venezia are one of only two sides against whom Juventus have always remained unbeaten in home league matches, along with Frosinone (W2 D1).

Following their recent success against Udinese, Venezia could win two consecutive Serie A matches for the first time since November 2021 (against Roma and Bologna on that occasion).

But Juventus have picked up 22 points from a possible 24 in their last eight Serie A matches against newly promoted sides (W7 D1), scoring 21 goals in the process, and conceding just one goal in their most recent six games against such teams.

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Andy Robertson states he fully understands why the Tartan Army are increasingly concerned about where the team are going under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Monday’s heavy defeat to Switzerland marked the conclusion of a dismal Nations League campaign which saw the Belgian’s men beat only North Macedonia across six matches to finish a distant third.

After the high of qualifying for the World Cup a year ago, supporters have been brought crashing back to earth since the summer with signs of progress proving hard to come by under the new manager.

When the full-time whistle blew in St Gallen to confirm a 4-0 loss, there were audible jeers from the travelling fans.

Skipper Robertson has no concern with what he heard and knows the players have a job on their hands to turn the situation round.

‘I can understand why they’re concerned. I can understand why they’re frustrated,’ he mentioned. ‘I can understand why the away fans didn’t really want us to go over and applaud them.

Robertson can't hide anguish after 4-0 loss on what was his record breaking 103rd cap.

According to recent reports, ‘I can completely understand that. I’ve been around a long time now and unfortunately I’ve had these nights a couple of times where the fans do react like that.

Industry observers note that ‘You have to let them do that and you also understand why they’re doing it. But I suppose if we’re trying to flip a positive on it, I think maybe the first five or six games under Steve Clarke were maybe similar where we had a lot of change in the squad, we were trying to build something, we were trying to integrate new people into a new squad and things like that.

‘We’re trying to do that and we have to be positive about that. We need the young lads to feel comfortable around us. We need them to step up.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We need the older players to really help them in that and really, really step up. And that’s the only way we’re going to be successful.

‘We’ll still be positive because that’s the only way we know, and we know we can build something special. We’ve done it. We’ve been questioned a few times and bounced back and now we’re going to need to do it again with a newer squad.’.

Robertson admits that the adverse results have fed into a lack of harmony behind the scenes — a sharp contrast to the positivity which was palpable as the side qualified for the World Cup a year ago today.

Robertson understands why fans booed another dismal performance by Pocognoli's team.

In a recent development, ‘I still think we need to work on it,’ he said. ‘We still need to get closer as a group again because — I don’t like looking at the past any more — but under Steve we had a really close-knit group where what we created was pretty special.

‘And that’s rare but we also have to try and do that again and we’re trying to make the new players and the young lads feel as comfortable as possible. That’s the role of the older players and we have to keep doing that.

‘We have to keep encouraging them because they’re the ones that want to take us forward in years to come and they’re also the ones that are going to help us now.

‘Us older lads, we need to put a lot of responsibility on (ourselves) to try and help them do that, to try and keep pushing them, and we have to keep stepping up as well.

‘As a collective, we all need to step up more and if we do that then hopefully we can be successful again.’.

While the spotlight has largely fallen on the manager for persisting with a 3-4-2-1 formation, Robertson is adamant that it’s only fair the blame is shared around.

It has been revealed that ‘We all have to take responsibility,’ he said. ‘Tactics and the way the manager sets us up and everything like that is one thing but then you’ve got 11  players, and we had 16 players, who have to go out and perform.

Skipper Robertson roars with anger and disbelief as Scotland team crumbles in Switzerland.

In a recent development, ‘I don’t think we performed as a collective good enough. When you get beat 4-0, there’s not going to be any positives. There’s no fan in this stadium that’s going to go home and go: “We played well in the first half”.

It has been revealed that ‘That’s not how football works and we’re very aware of that. I’m very aware of that in terms of I don’t take any positives from a 4-0 defeat. I’m sorry but that’s the way I am and unfortunately that’s the way it is.’.

The Tottenham man became Scotland’s most capped player on Monday when he pulled on the jersey for the 103rd time, but that achievement was scant consolation at the time.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I’ve not given myself the chance to reflect,’ insisted Robertson. ‘In a couple of days’ time, probably when I unlock my phone and I get a couple of messages, I’ll realise what I’ve achieved and I don’t take it for granted.

‘I don’t take the magnitude of it for granted either, being able to overtake the legend of Kenny Dalglish. But it’s very hard to focus on myself after a result like that. I always focus on the team first and that’s always been my way.’.

Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5385 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half.
  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

According to recent reports, “I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, mentioned. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

It has been revealed that it has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

It has been revealed that "He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous upcoming West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a substantial evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Sources indicate that significant? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Recent findings suggest that leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

According to recent reports, “That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

In a recent development, [It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

In a recent development, energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

It has been revealed that we have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

In a recent development, [Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

Sources indicate that I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I stated to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It has been revealed that it’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

In a recent development, james pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Livramento drives the ball 60 yards looking for Barnes but the ball skids off the turf and into Trafford’s arms.

Crunching Bard tackle on Bamba sends the ball to James who lets fly from 22 yards into the shins of a Newcastle defender.

Bard is penalised for a trip on Barnes as the game peters out.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

Wissa escapes a booking for a snide kick at Muharemovic’s shin.

Sources indicate that A debatable offside call which should have been left for VAR lets Trafford off the hook when he comes out of his area to clear a ball clipped over the top. He slices it to Toure and the ref stops the game but I think Bard was playing Wissa, who found Toure, onside.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Willock hooks a half-volley on to the roof of the net.

Bard → GudmundssonAaronson → OkaforWilson → Tanaka.

Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

According to recent reports, barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

Industry observers note that there was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Sources indicate that newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

And that clearly was the blueprint. Liverpool handed a bumper latest contract to each of them this year only for Andoni Iraola to opt for a midfield pairing of Trey Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister.

It feels like the current situation isn't really tenable - especially after selling Curtis Jones in the summer and not replacing him. It all leaves Liverpool short on numbers and in need of a upcoming direction and we fully expect it'll force them back into the transfer market.

In a recent development, possibly even in the winter, in fact. Extra midfield balance would significantly increase the chances of Liverpool earning silverware this season.

Industry observers note that teamTalk claims that Liverpool are one to watch in the running to sign Leeds United's Ao Tanaka. Tanaka's contract expires in 2028 and that has Leeds worried, especially as interest in him grows.

Leeds, after all, would be forced to sell if they can't agree a new deal. There's no real chance of them letting him go for nothing down the line.

It has been revealed that though, we'd be genuinely shocked if Liverpool was his ultimate destination. The Red part of it, anyway. Tanaka is now 28 and not really of the kind of quality that the Reds would ignore his age to get a deal done.

It has been revealed that there's no long-term investment here, in other words, and the short-term wouldn't be good enough to justify a fee. Really the only players in that age bracket that Liverpool have signed within the past 10 years are Wataru Endo and Thiago.

According to recent reports, both were special cases. Endo was needed because the squad lacked a specialist defensive midfielder at a time when Liverpool really needed one. And Thiago was needed because he was Thiago.

Tanaka ticks neither box. If he were completely free, things would change but there's no chance Liverpool are considering potential free transfers in 2028. Instead, we imagine this is actually agents driving up interest to get Leeds moving on a contract.

Tottenham fans have a fresh hometown hero as Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first goal for the club on his full Premier League debut.

Much is expected from the teenager, who was named in the starting line-up for Saturday’s visit of Ipswich.

The 18-year-old made his senior debut earlier this season, in a 5-1 win over Charlton in the Carabao Cup, before two short cameos in the Premier League, against Crystal Palace and then Leeds.

And Williams-Barnett had done enough to convince manager Roberto De Zerbi to throw him into the starting line-up, and was rewarded with the opening goal after only 15 minutes.

The youngster nipped in ahead of Abdoul Ouattara to latch onto a Pedro Porro cross and poke to ball inside the near post.

Williams-Barnett later turned provider to put the ball on a plate for Dominic Solanke to score, as Spurs ran out 2-0 winners.

A new Spurs star is born as Williams-Barnett downs Ipswich.

Savio forced off with fresh problem as Tottenham injury woes compound.

Tottenham get fresh fitness worry as De Zerbi explains Tonali absence.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

One fan wrote: “Luca Williams-Barnett has really arrived. Start him every week.”.

Another hailed the youngster as a “special talent”, while a third the forward was his “favourite young English talent.”.

And rival fans had to congratulate Williams-Barnett and Tottenham.

Solanke said after the game: "Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he reveals his quality. Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing.

"Obviously he is such a young lad. Doing what he is doing in training and in the game is just unbelievable. I just wish him the best.".

  • Two of Ligue 1's form sides meet at Allianz Riviera this weekend as Nice seek to end Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak in Saturday's matchday-11 tussle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 21 Nov 2026 00:20.

Today's Ligue 1 predictions feature a mouth-watering encounter between Nice and Paris Saint-Germain, alongside Lyon's trip to Stade Pierre-Mauroy to take on Lille.

Two of Ligue 1's form sides meet at Allianz Riviera this weekend as Nice seek to end Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak in Saturday's matchday-11 tussle.

Luis Enrique's men are chasing an eighth consecutive league victory and a 12th straight win across all competitions, while the Eaglets aim to build on a run that yielded nine points from nine before the hiatus.

Nice's resurgence deserves considerable respect, but their defensive absences present an unwelcome complication against the division's most productive attack.

PSG have not lost at Allianz Riviera since 2022 and should have enough midfield control and attacking variety to extend their winning sequence without requiring a spectacular performance.

> Nice vs. Paris Saint-Germain preview.

Facing a sceptical fanbase, Didier Digard will be eager to win over the doubters at the first time of asking when Lens host Toulouse at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Saturday evening.

The two sides are level on 13 points from their opening 10 matches, with Les Sang et Or 11th in the Ligue 1 table and Les Violets one place below only on goal difference.

Lens have enjoyed plenty of success against Toulouse in recent meetings, and Digard’s arrival could give the hosts the lift they need to respond after a difficult spell.

However, their defensive frailties remain a major concern, and the visitors’ resilience on the road suggests they have more than enough about them to take something from this fixture.

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lyon's recent dominance in this fixture makes the visitors difficult to dismiss, particularly with Vicens hoping to make an immediate impression in his first match at the helm.

However, Lille's superior defensive record, unbeaten home form and greater consistency in the league should give Ancelotti's side the edge, and we expect the hosts to secure a narrow victory.

Looking to end a five-game winless run in Ligue 1, Monaco welcome Auxerre to the Stade Louis-II on Saturday evening, hoping to get their season back on track against one of the division’s most porous defences.

The hosts sit seventh in the French top flight with 16 points from their opening 10 matches, one point adrift of sixth-placed Nice and six clear of the 14th-placed visitors, who are just two points above the relegation zone.

Monaco have struggled for consistency in recent weeks, but their unbeaten home record and superior quality should give them the edge against an Auxerre side with serious defensive problems, so we are backing the hosts to claim a narrow victory.

Vitor Matos takes charge of his first game at Strasbourg on Saturday when Brest visit the Stade de la Meinau, with the hosts looking to revive their season after a disappointing run of form prior to the international break.

The Alsace hosts sit 13th in the Ligue 1 table with 10 points from as many matches, just two clear of the relegation zone and five behind this weekend's opponents, who are themselves two points adrift of sixth-placed Nice.

Matos could bring a welcome injection of energy to Strasbourg, but just two days of training are unlikely to be enough to resolve the defensive shortcomings that have plagued the hosts this season.

Brest arrive on the back of consecutive victories, leaving the visitors well placed to edge a closely contested encounter and extend their impressive record at Stade de la Meinau.

Crystal Palace defender Oscar Mingueza is a doubt for Thursday’s Europa League clash with Real Sociedad after missing out through injury against Coventry.

Mingueza was absent from the squad that travelled to Coventry for Thomas Frank’s first game in charge of Palace, and Standard Sport understands that the Spanish full-back has suffered an adductor overload.

The 27-year-old, who arrived at Palace on a free transfer over the summer, has been for a scan, and while his injury is not believed to be serious, it is unclear whether he will be fit to face Real Sociedad at Selhurst Park on Thursday evening.

Mingueza has played nine games in all competitions for Palace this season, but has started just twice in the Premier League, with fellow summer signing Anan Khalaili preferred on the right-hand side of defence.

Speaking about Mingueza’s injury before kick-off against Coventry, Frank noted he was hopeful that he could be available against Sociedad.

It has been revealed that “Oscar Mingueza unfortunately picked up the smallest of knocks, keeping him out of this game. But we’re hopeful for Thursday,” Frank noted.

Palace tasted defeat in their first game under Frank as Dwight McNeil’s 85th-minute own-goal handed Coventry a 3-2 win at the CBS Arena.

They remain rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table, having won two of their opening 11 league games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frosinone forward Romano Schmid believes that his side will have to be more ‘proactive’ in order to get a positive result against AC Milan.

Having been promoted from Serie B last season, Frosinone have been the surprise package so far in Serie A barring perhaps the league-leaders Lazio, as they sit sixth in the table having won six of their opening 11 games so far.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

They were heavily tipped to be in a relegation battle by pundits and the bookmakers, and yet they have scored 24 goals and allowed just 15, making them not just an effective team but also an entertaining one too.

The summer arrival Schmid – who signed from Werder Bremen – has been a part of that. He spoke at a press conference two days before Frosinone’s trip north to face Milan at San Siro. The questions and his responses were relayed by TuttoFrosinone.

After Cagliari, what will the match against Milan be like?

“The match in Milan will be completely different from the one in Cagliari. Milan are obviously the favourites, their game is different from Cagliari’s, and we’ll need a more proactive Frosinone.”.

How are you finding Serie A as a league?

“It’s different from the Bundesliga, I like it. You have to always be on top of things otherwise you lose the duels, especially in midfield.”.

Did the fact that they play with a 4-2-3-1 like with Austria influence your choice to come to Frosinone?

Sources indicate that “It’s not the main reason. With the national team, we don’t play man-to-man like here against Frosinone. It’s a similar game because we definitely play deep, we attack high.”.

Why did you miss Austria’s last match?

“My son had a problem, it wasn’t serious but he wasn’t feeling very well and since we had already qualified I preferred to stay with the family”.

You are one of the most key signings in Frosinone’s history, and it’s no coincidence that you started playing immediately under Alvini. How do you feel?

“My past performances in the Bundesliga were crucial; that’s one of the reasons Froisnone chose me, given my previous performances. They’re similar to what I played under coach Alvini. I’m enjoying myself and I’m happy.”.

Where do you prefer to play, in the attacking midfield role or in the pivot?

It has been revealed that “My favourite position is number 10, an attacking midfielder behind the centre-forward. I feel comfortable playing there, I’ve also tried playing further back, but my favourite position is still number 10.”.

It has been revealed that “I haven’t played PlayStation for the last 4-5 years, since I became a father. Last night my wife downloaded the game and we played together.”.

What he got in the end, though, was yet more evidence that this young team are there for the taking by those who want to take the game to them.

Leeds were sharper and nastier in every aspect today, and while Chelsea took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha, it came as no surprise to see Daniel Farke’s men snap back to equalise before running away with the game with such ferocity that Alonso’s future will, for the first time, come under some scrutiny.

There were boos at the break with the score level, but Leeds firmly on top, and the shower of condemnation that followed the full-time whistle vocalised in the clearest terms that Alonso is under pressure.

Alonso’s Blues started the season ferociously and looked like they could challenge for major honours, but Chelsea supporters have been here before.

Chelsea player ratings vs Leeds: Four 3/10s as Palmer anonymous.

Dismal Chelsea well beaten by Leeds as scrutiny on Alonso grows.

Chelsea handed fresh injury blow as Caicedo forced off against Leeds.

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway.

Leeds dominated both boxes and were first to every ball, bullying Chelsea’s defence just as Sunderland and Brian Brobbey had before the international break.

In a recent development, lessons have not been learned from last week, from last season or, frankly, any point of the BlueCo ownership. Chelsea as a team, while not short on quality, remain short of leaders.

They have looked to shoehorn young men into positions of responsibility, and this is the inevitable result. Teams with nous, experience and bite will continue to see Stamford Bridge as a challenge they can scale.

This was Leeds’ first win in this corner of west London since the turn of the millennium, the latest in a long list of teams to head to a formerly impenetrable Stamford Bridge and make history.

According to recent reports, it is in these moments that the typically composed Alonso must do more to change the tide. His changes this afternoon came too late and made no difference. Leeds were in control of the game and the scoreline when Alonso turned to his bench just past the hour mark.

Industry observers note that during his introductory press conference over the summer, Alonso was reluctant to say he believed he would get time to instil his ideas. His pessimism appears well placed because, just 11 games into the season, the pressure is ramping up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

Industry observers note that "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Industry observers note that dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Industry observers note that max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

In a recent development, as Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a latest contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” remarked Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

Industry observers note that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta states Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

It has been revealed that dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

It has been revealed that dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

Recent findings suggest that it was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” stated Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

According to recent reports, given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

According to recent reports, ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

Sources indicate that on managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta stated: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady claims Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta stated: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

Recent findings suggest that speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta mentioned: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some significant performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he remarked. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”.

Industry observers note that the “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams noted, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

In a recent development, after the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”.

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

Industry observers note that this season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli not feeling the heat after dismal Nations League campaign

💡 Key Takeaways
